note: Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree on all 55). Guides are written for this entry, in its own words, and cite their sources beside each trophy. 28 of the 55 are hidden on PlayStation until earned; all 55 are single-player, none are online, and the set takes about 200 hours (PowerPyx, via EGamers).

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The Platinum pops the moment the 54th other trophy unlocks — there is no separate task. Work the roadmap in order: story first, side-character finals, then the free-roam cleanup, with A Long Road (100% completion) last. PowerPyx rates the whole set 4 out of 10 and about 200 hours, and KeenGamer's roadmap agrees one playthrough is enough with no online play needed.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission. Play through the prologue as the story directs you — the first job together — and the trophy pops when the mission ends. Unmissable; it is the first story trophy of the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Before you leave the chapter, do Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house — PowerPyx and GTABase flag it as the one interaction that may be missable later (see Positive Mental Attitude). Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter: the game has no mission replay.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The hardest trophy in the set, by both PowerPyx and GTABase (via EGamers). The in-game checklist has 35 tasks; PowerPyx puts the requirement at roughly 60% of true completion, and the checklist must be finished after the story. Most of it comes from doing the other trophies — finish the story, all activities, collectibles and challenges, then mop up the checklist. KeenGamer's 100% section lists the required progress per activity. Do it last, right before the Platinum.
